title: SELECT: reading data

spans.text: “SELECT: reading data” is a tool for solving a concrete programming problem. Identify the input and desired result, then trace what role the construct plays in the example. Study it not only as syntax, but also for its effects on readability, correctness, resource use, and future changes.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
Returns product names and calculated prices ordered by name.

SELECT produces a result set. FROM names its source; listing columns explicitly is clearer and more stable than * when a schema changes. Use AS for a readable output alias. Without ORDER BY, row order is not guaranteed.

Key line: `SELECT name, price_cents / 100.0 AS price`
What it does: Returns product names and calculated prices ordered by name.
Why it is used: Select only the columns you need; this improves readability and reduces surprises when a schema changes.
If omitted or changed: AS renames a result column; it does not rename the stored table column.

spans.title: Common mistake
spans.text: Converting prices to floating point can introduce rounding; preserve exact stored values for financial calculations.
